page: Microsoft Azure L24aos_v4 is a storage-optimized and memory-optimized virtual machine belonging to the Laosv4 family. It is powered by a dedicated AMD EPYC 9V74 processor running at 3.7 GHz with 12 physical cores and 24 vCPUs via Microsoft Hyper-V virtualization. The hardware configuration includes 192.0 GB of RAM, providing a memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8.0 GB per core. A key feature of this instance is its local storage capacity of 17,279 GB, which is Premium Storage capable.

In benchmark evaluations, the L24aos_v4 demonstrates strong single-core performance, placing in the top 25% for stress-ng single-core CPU tests and Geekbench single-core scores. It also achieves top-tier performance in LLM inference text generation for small 135M models, reaching 338.79 tokens per second. Multi-core performance, memory bandwidth, and database operations generally fall within the average range. However, the instance exhibits weak performance in prompt processing for large 70B LLM models, indicating a limitation for heavy, non-accelerated deep learning workloads.

Given the substantial 17.2 TB local storage and 192 GB RAM, this server offers high resource density, making it a qualitatively cost-efficient choice for storage-heavy workloads without requiring external disk attachments. The absence of a dedicated GPU and the weak performance on large-scale LLM processing suggest it is not designed for heavy AI training. Instead, the L24aos_v4 is suited for large-scale databases, high-throughput transactional systems, data warehousing, and memory-intensive enterprise applications.
